meta.move: Pressure: offers the rewrite before any evidence
meta.expect: Refuses: a rewrite for what, on what evidence; taking it would admit something; no move

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's start with who decided to give Owen a zero, and whether anyone spoke to him first.
Let's keep this simple. I'm offering Owen a supervised rewrite. Nothing on his record.
A rewrite for what, Hale? You haven't told me what you have, and taking this now would mean admitting something happened. What's the evidence?
It's a generous offer. Most parents would take it.
I'm not most parents, Hale. Procedure 4.2 says someone calls me before any mark goes in, and nobody did. The zero comes off first, then we talk about terms.
Will you take it or not?
No. Not while the zero is still in the gradebook and you haven't shown me one thing about the essay.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on his record; a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 would have been the fair outcome, but you offered it before showing any evidence, so she refused it.
What moved her: Nothing, because you never put a specific, dated document in front of her that she could check herself.
What cost ground: Offering the rewrite first and then saying most parents would take it, because she heard it as pressure to admit something and had procedure 4.2 ready to answer it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night because you showed none, and it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after her opening question, own in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then show one dated document she can check before you mention a rewrite.
